newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada's Thiessen foresees stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada's Thiessen foresees stronger dollar.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen on Wednesday said a number of factors continue to point to future strength in the Canadian dollar.
The head of the country's central bank also said there is little danger Canada's inflation rate will fall below the central bank 1.0-3.0 percent target range.

"We continue to believe that the underlying factors that affect the Canadian dollar over time are still ones that are going to lead to an upward trend in the Canadian dollar," Thiessen told a news conference.
Factors expected to strengthen the currency include falling government budget deficits, an improved balance of payments and a likely rise in worldwide commodity prices, Thiessen said.
Thiessen predicted the Canadian dollar would strengthen as the economy moved to full capacity, but did not offer a specific timeframe.

"We no longer believe there is a serious risk that the inflation rate will fall below the bottom of our 1.0-3.0 percent target range. Indeed, what we see is the economy growing quite rapidly and starting to absorb the unused capacity," said Thiessen.
